name: Apiaká
confidence_why: Pádua 2007, the only phonological description of Apiaká, and Sousa 2017, the only grammar, give no rule for word stress and their transcriptions mark it on final, penultimate and once initial syllables without comment, so no placement can be stated and SAPhon (built on Pádua) lists no suprasegmental at all.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote confirmed verbatim in the Pádua 2007 text we hold layer and PDF at the stated section; only the printed-page locator is off by one (29-30, not 28-29). (2) The classification not determinable rests on the only phonological description of the language (2007 MA dissertation), cross-checked against the only grammar (Sousa 2017 PhD), both. neither states where stress falls, and Pádua's own transcriptions/underlying forms mark stress lexically on final, penult and (once) initial syllables without comment, so no rule can be read off. (3) No better source exists: Glottolog has one descriptive ref, SAPhon lists no suprasegmentals, CrossRef shows no post-2017 linguistic work, and the language has effectively no fluent speakers left, so an instrumental or prosodic study is not to be expected. sources.note: Its orthographic wordlist writes an acute accent on the stressed vowel (ywaté, arasá, nhandú vs siwerapára, sawapúku per Sousa 2017:93), the only place Pádua commits stress to an orthography; the full list is already reproduced in the held Sousa 2017 annex (Lista 11, the text layerff.), so the original adds only any orthographic note on the accent convention.
